headline: Forkast News reports that the open-source Home Assistant smart-home software is adding a free built-in connection that lets AI assistants of the owner's choice control home devices.
score_reason: Useful for smart-home users, but single-source, pre-release and partly commentary.
importance_line: Smart-home owners could use any AI assistant to control devices at no charge, though this rests on one outlet's preview and it raises security and privacy questions.
summary: Forkast News reports that Home Assistant 2026.10, due on 7 Oct, builds in MCP (the Model Context Protocol, a standard that lets AI assistants use other software's tools) so owners can connect an AI of their choice to their home devices through a one-click setting. Forkast says the feature is free and runs locally, contrasts it with Google's $20-a-month Home MCP service, and warns that giving third-party agents control of a home needs care over privacy and data access.
notes: Single outlet, partly opinion; Google pricing and other comparisons are Forkast's. Apple HomePad claims not repeated.
